first_step_test: A loose three-panel zigzag outer contour gives the reader the width and fold positions of a folded paper map immediately.

source.notes: First five-panel sheet rejected as too sparse; second six-panel sheet rejected because finish lacked enough tactile folded-paper character. Third iteration pending.

final_elements.description: One uneven landscape rectangle in the final position.

final_elements.name: winding route
final_elements.description: One dotted winding route across the three panels.

final_elements.name: mountain pair
final_elements.description: Two small separate triangular mountain icons in upper-left map area.

frames.instruction: Draw one broad landscape rectangle with gently uneven edges. Keep its top and bottom almost parallel.

frames.visible_job: Add two paper creases inside the fixed outline.
frames.instruction: Inside the rectangle, draw two widely spaced vertical zigzag creases. Keep the same outer paper edge; the folds divide it into three panels.

frames.visible_job: Add one route crossing all three panels.
frames.instruction: From the lower left, draw one broken winding route across both creases to the upper right. Leave room at both endpoints for markers.

frames.visible_job: Add two peaks and one river bend in fixed places.
frames.instruction: Above the route on the left panel, draw two small mountain peaks. Below the route on the right panel, draw one short curved river bend.

frames.visible_job: Add two endpoint symbols and one compass rose.
frames.instruction: Put a small open circle at the route’s left end and a tiny triangle at the right end. In the open middle panel draw a little four-point compass rose.

final_step.visible_job: Add pale pencil shading to the existing folds and restrained color to established route, peaks, and river.
final_step.instruction: Shade one side of each established crease with light HB. Trace the existing dotted route in muted red, tint the two peaks moss green, and the river pale blue; keep the paper mostly white.
adds: shading and color on established marks

visual_review.first_step_observation: The first saved square crop shows one broad, slightly wavy landscape paper rectangle only. Its stable outer edges and roomy interior give a beginner a clear first shape.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: Six saved crops keep the paper outline, two fixed fold creases and one dotted route, then add exactly two peaks, one river, endpoint circle and triangle, and one four-point compass before final graphite and colored-pencil shading. No temporary guides were used or removed; no unexplained structural movement or erasure is visible.

transitions.observed_addition: The same wavy outer paper edge stays at the same anchors; two separate zigzag creases divide it into three panels.
transitions.instruction_match: The second instruction places exactly two creases inside the established outline.

transitions.observed_addition: The outer edge and both folds persist; one separated dotted trail begins low left, crosses both creases and ends high right.
transitions.instruction_match: The third instruction draws the one dotted trail across the three panels.

transitions.observed_addition: The map, folds and dotted route persist; two distinct triangular peaks appear high left and one two-line river bend appears low right.
transitions.instruction_match: The fourth instruction adds the two peaks and river away from the route.

transitions.observed_addition: The same peaks, river, route, folds and outer edge persist; one open circle caps the left route end, one triangle caps the right end and a four-point compass appears in the open center panel.
transitions.instruction_match: The fifth instruction locates both endpoints and the compass in the blank middle space.

transitions.observed_addition: All nine named landmarks retain their positions; soft graphite shades the paper folds, existing route dots turn muted red, the two peaks gain green and the river blue.
transitions.instruction_match: The final instruction shades and colors only established paper planes and marks.
